title: Run
description: A recorded run: the commands an operator sent to a chip, in time order. Written by operator/, replayed by twin/.

chip_spec.description: Repo-relative path of the chip spec this run used, e.g. chip/placeholder_chip_spec.json. The twin loads the chip from here.

placeholder.description: true when the protocol or chip spec it was made from is a placeholder.

sizing.description: Optional. operator/sizing.py chip_sizing() for this chip (capsule count, trap area and volume needed vs available, channel widths). Shown in the twin's sizing panel.

simulated_hardware.description: true when the run used the virtual chip (SIMULATED HARDWARE): every 'true' value is from the simulation.

loop.description: closed: sensors corrected the model during the run.

scenario.description: The scenario file this run used (sensors, reality, faults).

run_parameters.description: Values of the chip's run parameters for this run, e.g. {"variant": "control"}.

summary.description: Final exchange %, capsule recovery, reagent used, alerts, recoveries and belief-vs-truth drift.

transcript.description: Repo-relative path of the operator's tool-call transcript (for scripted replay).

report.description: Repo-relative path of the Markdown report.

log.description: Operator log: plans (with the candidate table), safety results, alerts, model updates, re-plans, pauses.

t_s.description: Protocol time when the command starts, in seconds.

duration_s.description: How long the command takes, in seconds.

narration.description: One sentence shown in the twin's narration panel.

protocol_step.description: The protocol step this command carries out, or null.

recovery.description: true for a recovery action (e.g. back-flush after an alert).

plan_args.description: The full plan this segment executed (flow, washes, soak ...).

slices.description: Time slices: predicted, measured and (simulation only) true values, error, believed and true state.

measured.description: Readings taken during this command (e.g. Module 1b's counter: cells_per_ul, viability).
